title: Collapsing Structural/Validation Failures to Booleans
pattern: Returning a simple `bool` from a validation or typing function instead of a rich error type explaining *what* failed and *where*.
why_bad: It throws away all diagnostic information. Downstream UI forms or logs cannot report whether the street was missing or the postal code was of incorrect length; they only know that "something" failed.
detection: Functions with names containing `validate`, `verify`, or `check` that accept domain inputs and return `bool`.
source: *Types and Programming Languages* by Benjamin C. Pierce (p. 204, Section 14.1).
